question.problem: Find the horizontal asymptote of the function $f(x)=\frac{6{x}^{5}}{2{x}^{9}+{x}^{4}+9x}.$
question.worked_solution:
The horizontal asymptote is $y={lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x).$ To find the horizontal asymptote, we apply the usual procedure of dividing the numerator and denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{9}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{6{x}^{5}}{2{x}^{9}+{x}^{4}+9x} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{6{x}^{5}}{{x}^{9}})}{(\frac{2{x}^{9}}{{x}^{9}}+\frac{{x}^{4}}{{x}^{9}}+\frac{9x}{{x}^{9}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{6}{{x}^{4}})}{(2+\frac{1}{{x}^{5}}+\frac{9}{{x}^{8}})} \\  & =\frac{0}{2+0+0} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the horizontal asymptote is $y=0.$
